sources.title: Adobe — Speed
sources.direct_supported_claim: Temporal speed can be inspected and adjusted independently from a motion path; Easy Ease is a particular velocity/influence setting, not a quality verdict.
sources.uncertainty: Graph shape must be judged at delivery speed; values are not portable presets.
sources.scope: newly source-verified research; not imported FCWM lesson

sources.title: Adobe — Keyframe interpolation
sources.direct_supported_claim: Temporal interpolation and spatial interpolation answer different questions; hold interpolation preserves an outgoing value until the next keyframe.
sources.uncertainty: No claim of identical interpolation across engines.
sources.scope: newly source-verified research; not imported FCWM lesson

sources.title: Adobe — Animating text
sources.direct_supported_claim: Text animator selectors can operate on characters, words or lines; including spaces changes selection progression.
sources.uncertainty: Does not establish universal reading speeds or multilingual shaping parity.
sources.scope: newly source-verified research; not imported FCWM lesson

sources.title: Adobe — Responsive design
sources.direct_supported_claim: Protected temporal regions retain duration while other portions stretch.
sources.uncertainty: Temporal protection does not prove automatic aspect-ratio layout adaptation.
sources.scope: newly source-verified research; not imported FCWM lesson

sources.title: Adobe — Cameras, lights, and points of interest
sources.direct_supported_claim: Camera framing depends on geometric parameters; AE aperture controls depth of field without changing exposure.
sources.uncertainty: Physical camera and Blender exposure equivalence is not established.
sources.scope: newly source-verified research; not imported FCWM lesson

sources.title: Adobe — Layer properties
sources.direct_supported_claim: Parenting makes transforms relative to a parent but does not inherit opacity; the anchor point controls transform pivots.
sources.uncertainty: A DOM compositing group is not automatically equivalent.
sources.scope: newly source-verified research; not imported FCWM lesson

sources.title: Adobe — Precomposing, nesting, and pre-rendering
sources.direct_supported_claim: Raster/vector render orders and collapsed transformations affect nesting, effect results and 3D interaction.
sources.uncertainty: No assertion that CSS grouping or a canvas layer reproduces AE collapse transformations.
sources.scope: newly source-verified research; not imported FCWM lesson

sources.title: Adobe — Track Mattes and Traveling Mattes
sources.direct_supported_claim: Its explicit matte table states full alpha produces opacity in a non-inverted alpha matte.
sources.uncertainty: Introduction contradicts the table about increasing transparency. Use the table plus W3C corroboration; do not trust isolated wording.
sources.scope: newly source-verified research; not imported FCWM lesson

sources.title: Adobe — Assorted animation tools
sources.direct_supported_claim: Motion blur depends on shutter angle, phase and temporal sampling; transform blur does not discover motion internal to source footage.
sources.uncertainty: Optical-flow blur and transform sampling are distinct methods.
sources.scope: newly source-verified research; not imported FCWM lesson

sources.title: Dan Ebberts — Realistic Bounce and Overshoot
sources.direct_supported_claim: Distinguishes decaying oscillation from successive ballistic bounces, including their different timing behavior.
sources.uncertainty: Practitioner mathematical treatment, not permission to copy expressions or a universal taste rule.
sources.scope: newly source-verified research; not imported FCWM lesson

sources.title: School of Motion — Eye Tracing in Animation
sources.direct_supported_claim: Jacob Richardson and Ryan Plummer discuss guiding attention and connecting focal positions across a sequence.
sources.uncertainty: Embedded videos were not watched; no eye-tracking experiment was performed.
sources.scope: newly source-verified research; not imported FCWM lesson

sources.title: IBM Design — Classic principles
sources.direct_supported_claim: IBM applies staging, anticipation, overlap and timing to its own restrained animation language.
sources.uncertainty: Brand-specific aesthetic choices must not become universal restrictions.
sources.scope: newly source-verified research; not imported FCWM lesson

sources.title: Remotion — interpolate()
sources.direct_supported_claim: Boundary behavior is configured separately with extrapolateLeft and extrapolateRight.
sources.uncertainty: Live docs may exceed installed 4.0.530; basic clamp behavior was separately audited, new features were not.
sources.scope: newly source-verified research; not imported FCWM lesson

sources.title: Remotion — spring()
sources.direct_supported_claim: A spring is evaluated from frame and fps with physical-style parameters and optional duration/overshoot controls.
sources.uncertainty: Parameter names do not imply equivalence to AE expressions, CSS springs or other solvers.
sources.scope: newly source-verified research; not imported FCWM lesson

sources.title: GSAP — CustomEase
sources.direct_supported_claim: CustomEase creates easing from supplied curve data.
sources.uncertainty: Marketing language about freedom is not a numerical stability or cross-engine parity guarantee.
sources.scope: newly source-verified research; not imported FCWM lesson

sources.title: GSAP — seek()
sources.direct_supported_claim: seek changes position without changing paused/reversed state; callbacks are suppressed by default.
sources.uncertainty: Seeking alone does not establish deterministic scene state.
sources.scope: newly source-verified research; not imported FCWM lesson

sources.title: W3C — Understanding SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions
sources.direct_supported_claim: Level AAA criterion concerns disabling nonessential motion animation triggered by interaction.
